tagline: Down the Arkansas under Harvard, Yale and Princeton.
intro: From Granite, an old gold camp on the Arkansas River between the Mosquito and Sawatch ranges, the byway follows the river south along the foot of the Sawatch, paved for all 57 miles. To the west stand the fourteeners, Mounts Harvard, Yale and Princeton among them. Buena Vista comes along, then Nathrop, then Salida, where the river leaves the valley.

Salida is Spanish for exit, named for the spot where the Arkansas flows out into Bighorn Sheep Canyon. When the railroad built its station there in 1880 and bypassed nearby Cleora, it is said the people of Cleora simply moved to Salida.

moments.title: Granite
moments.text: Granite held the county seat until one November night in 1880, when men from Buena Vista borrowed a locomotive and hauled off the records, the furniture and the still-warm stove.

moments.title: Buena Vista
moments.text: Alsina Dearheimer chose the name and also specified how to say it, BEW-nuh VIST-uh, though many residents just call the town BV.

moments.title: Mount Antero
moments.text: A forest road from near the ghost town of St. Elmo climbs toward the summit of a peak with one of the highest concentrations of aquamarine in the country.

sources.label: Colorado Department of Transportation, Collegiate Peaks
